questions.problem:
Which of the following are affine transformations?

I. ${T}_{1}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}uv \\ u+v\end{aligned}]$

II. ${T}_{2}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}v \\ 2v-u\end{aligned}]$

III. ${T}_{3}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}-{u}^{2} \\ 2u+v\end{aligned}]$
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

With this in mind, let's look at each transformation in turn.

- Transformation ${T}_{1}$ is not affine since it contains the cross term $uv.$

- Transformation ${T}_{2}$ is affine. Notice that ${T}_{2}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}v \\ 2v-u\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}v \\ -u+2v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

In fact, the transformation ${T}_{1}$ is a linear transformation.

- Transformation ${T}_{3}$ is not affine since it contains the quadratic term ${u}^{2}.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "${T}_{2}$ only."

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}v-7u \\ 2v-u\end{aligned}].

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $\mathbf T:\mathbb R^2\rightarrow\mathbb R^2$ is a function of the form

$$
\mathbf x = A \mathbf u + \mathbf b,
$$

where $\mathbf x, \mathbf u,$ and $\mathbf b$ are column vectors in $\mathbb R^2,$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

With this in mind, let's look at each transformation in turn.

- Transformation $\mathbf{T}_1$ is affine. Notice that $\mathbf{T}_1$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u+v \\ v-2u+1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u+v \\ -2u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

- Transformation $\mathbf{T}_2$ is affine. Notice that $\mathbf{T}_2$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u-v \\ v-u\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u-v \\ -u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

In fact, the transformation $\mathbf{T}_2$ is a linear transformation.

- Transformation $\mathbf{T}_3$ is not affine since it contains the quadratic term $v^2.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$\mathbf{T}_1$ and $\mathbf{T}_2$ only."

Example: 
                    Finding the Parametric Representation of an Affine Transformation Given its Matrix Form
canonical_examples.problem:
The matrix form of the affine transformation

$$
x = 3u-v + \bbox[Gainsboro,2pt]{a}, \qquad y = u + \bbox[Gainsboro,2pt]{b}v + \bbox[Gainsboro,2pt]{c}
$$

is shown below. What is the value of $a+b+c?$
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14272296/assets/026d8214875c834de4ee242a8a94ca14958a0b097af6be4fc3605b1381e3d4ca.svg)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $\mathbf T:\mathbb R^2\rightarrow\mathbb R^2$ is a function of the form

$$
\mathbf x = A \mathbf u + \mathbf b,
$$

where $\mathbf x, \mathbf u,$ and $\mathbf b$ are column vectors in $\mathbb R^2,$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

We can carry out the matrix operations using the matrix form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}]}}\cdot \overset{u}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}}+\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3u-v \\ u-5v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3u-v+1 \\ u-5v\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding elements, we obtain

$$
x = 3u - v + \bbox[Gainsboro,2pt]{1}, \qquad y = u + (\bbox[Gainsboro,2pt]{-5})v + \bbox[Gainsboro,2pt]{0} \, .
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c = 1+(-5)+0 = -4.
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Representation of an Affine Transformation Given its Matrix Form

canonical_examples.name:
Example: 
                    Finding the Matrix Representation of an Affine Transformation Given its Parametric Form
canonical_examples.problem:
The matrix form of the affine transformation

$$
x = 5u + v - 6, \qquad y = 2u + 4v
$$

is shown below. What is the value of $a+b+c?$
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14272296/assets/840170751f28de915bdc62062fc421258cfa103da5d3458c26d48d98bfbf2ded.svg)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $\mathbf T:\mathbb R^2\rightarrow\mathbb R^2$ is a function of the form

$$
\mathbf x = A \mathbf u + \mathbf b,
$$

where $\mathbf x, \mathbf u,$ and $\mathbf b$ are column vectors in $\mathbb R^2,$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

First, notice that we can express the given transformation as
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14272296/assets/9d656e03589b24865e13de1c5d55b56be325fe69557beca982d082e2b302a7ee.svg)

Separating the constants and expressing the linear part as a product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5u+v-6 \\ 2u+4v\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5u+v \\ 2u+4v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c = 1+2+0 = 3.
$$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
An **affine transformation** $\mathbf T:\mathbb R^2\rightarrow\mathbb R^2$ is a function that can be expressed in the form

$$
\mathbf x = A \mathbf u + \mathbf b,
$$

where $\mathbf x, \mathbf u,$ and $\mathbf b$ are column vectors in $\mathbb R^2,$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix. 

Under this notation, 

- ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14272296/assets/2282e58771a8964c133f99f35b81a7d6231b39fb5819eb83cbebe03b0866e41f.svg) represents vectors belonging to the input space, and

- ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14272296/assets/78dc6723185a9c96588fc877808d56a04b5573b4b128b7b11998d361e73f0104.svg)  represents vectors belonging to the output space.

For example,

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14272296/assets/3707b2576fab47366e0230deb3d8fd9bcd48c612b3a20a324e3569b13d771028.svg)

is an affine transformation because it can be expressed in the form $\mathbf x = A\mathbf u + \mathbf b,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u-v+1 \\ 2u+v-3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u-v \\ 2u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

However, the transformation

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14272296/assets/cfb4bd470c0522d982d68f4e729fef7f05f9ace402b4b59bbd1585e5a7284097.svg)

is not affine since it contains the quadratic term $uv.$

Finally, note the following relationships between affine and linear transformations:

- A linear transformation $\mathbf x = A \mathbf u$ is a special case of an affine transformation with $\mathbf b = \mathbf 0.$

- For an affine transformation $\mathbf T$ given by $\mathbf x = A\mathbf u + \mathbf b,$ we say that $A$ is *the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with* $\mathbf T.$

tutorials.title: Introduction
tutorials.content:
An **affine transformation** $\mathbf T:\mathbb R^2\rightarrow\mathbb R^2$ is a function that can be expressed in the form

$$
\mathbf x = A \mathbf u + \mathbf b,
$$

where $\mathbf x, \mathbf u,$ and $\mathbf b$ are column vectors in $\mathbb R^2,$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix. 

Under this notation, 

- ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14272296/assets/2282e58771a8964c133f99f35b81a7d6231b39fb5819eb83cbebe03b0866e41f.svg) represents vectors belonging to the input space, and

- ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14272296/assets/78dc6723185a9c96588fc877808d56a04b5573b4b128b7b11998d361e73f0104.svg)  represents vectors belonging to the output space.

For example,

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14272296/assets/3707b2576fab47366e0230deb3d8fd9bcd48c612b3a20a324e3569b13d771028.svg)

is an affine transformation because it can be expressed in the form $\mathbf x = A\mathbf u + \mathbf b,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u-v+1 \\ 2u+v-3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u-v \\ 2u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

However, the transformation

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14272296/assets/cfb4bd470c0522d982d68f4e729fef7f05f9ace402b4b59bbd1585e5a7284097.svg)

is not affine since it contains the quadratic term $uv.$

Finally, note the following relationships between affine and linear transformations:

- A linear transformation $\mathbf x = A \mathbf u$ is a special case of an affine transformation with $\mathbf b = \mathbf 0.$

- For an affine transformation $\mathbf T$ given by $\mathbf x = A\mathbf u + \mathbf b,$ we say that $A$ is *the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with* $\mathbf T.$
